questions.q: In the lab scenario, why is accepting Basic Auth's risk not justified even though it's faster to configure?
options: Basic Auth cannot technically be attached to a REST Message's Authentication Profile
The job runs every 15 minutes indefinitely, repeatedly sending a real credential that has no expiration, and the partner explicitly offers a stronger option
The partner's API does not support HTTPS
Basic Auth is always rejected by ServiceNow's REST Message framework
questions.explain: The specific justification is the recurring, unattended, long-running nature of the job plus the availability of a stronger supported option — not a vague "OAuth is better" claim.

questions.q: Why does the scenario call for the Client Credentials grant rather than Authorization Code?
options: Client Credentials is always required for scheduled jobs regardless of the use case
Authorization Code cannot be used with REST Messages
There is no human user anywhere in the loop — the integration authenticates as itself, which is exactly what Client Credentials is for
Client Credentials grants never expire, unlike Authorization Code
questions.explain: Authorization Code represents a specific human user's consent; this scenario has no human user involved, so Client Credentials is the correct fit.

questions.q: Which three fields does the OAuth Entity record need before an OAuth Entity Profile can be built on top of it?
options: Username, password, and a base64 flag
A certificate, a private key, and a certificate authority name
An API key, a header name, and a scope list
Client ID, client secret, and the token endpoint URL
questions.explain: Those three values — client ID, client secret, and the token endpoint URL — are what the partner's API documentation provides and what the OAuth Entity record stores.

questions.q: Where does the finished OAuth Entity Profile actually get attached, tying it into the work from Chapter 2?
options: Into the REST Message's Authentication Profile field
Directly into the integration's business logic script, with no other configuration
Into the ServiceNow instance's global system properties
It cannot be attached to anything built in Chapter 2
questions.explain: The REST Message built in Chapter 2 has an Authentication Profile field — that's exactly where the OAuth Entity Profile gets wired in.

questions.q: Once the OAuth Entity Profile is attached to the REST Message, what does the integration's own script need to do to manage the access token?
options: Manually request a new token before every call
Catch 401 responses and re-authenticate by hand
Nothing — ServiceNow automatically requests, caches, and refreshes the token behind the scenes
Store the token in a scheduled job's own custom table
questions.explain: This is the practical payoff from Lesson 9: once the profile is wired in, token lifecycle management happens automatically, with nothing added to the integration's script.
